blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — The World Bank cut its 2027 growth forecast for the Philippines, describing the country as an “outlier” in East Asia and the Pacific as war-driven pressures weigh on growth and the economy struggles to benefit from the global artificial intelligence (AI) boom. In its East Asia and Pacific Update released Tuesday, the Washington-based institution kept its 3.7 percent growth forecast for the Philippines this year but cut its 2027 outlook by 0.4 percentage point to 5.2 percent.
